text:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up: saw a slow, steady resident-size increase on a long-running streaming chat + tool-loop reproducer. ~120MB/hr on a 32GB instance, no OOM but growth doesn't plateau. Attaching quick logs and what I ran so we can triage.

kevin: curious — is this definitely KV residency vs general heap fragmentation? any jemalloc or pmap dumps? :eyes:

maria (eng-runtime): initial data:
- run: local devbox, 8h streaming chat with tool loop (agent calls every 30s), batch_size=4, kernel_profile=auto
- pmap snapshots: 
  02:00: pmap total 32,040 kB rss (baseline)
  06:00: pmap total 33,080 kB rss
  10:00: pmap total 35,120 kB rss
  16:00: pmap total 36,080 kB rss
- jemalloc stats after 16h: active 1.9GB, allocated 1.5GB, metadata ~150MB, retained ~300MB
- KV metrics: active_slots=1.2M, pinned_slots=18k, page_reads=high (spike during tool calls), evictions/sec ~0.4

I also grabbed a short malloc backtrace sample and a perf record (low sampling) — linking: https://internal.srv/tmp/2749990000-flame.svg (CL: not public)

olga: can you paste the exact KV debug counters? especially "last_access" age hist and pagechain lengths. suspect slot aging or cross-session pinning.

maria (eng-runtime): pasted counters below:
```
kv_total_slots: 1250000
kv_active_slots: 1212345
kv_pinned_slots: 18342
kv_page_reads: 238451
kv_page_writes: 19241
kv_evictions: 34567
kv_eviction_time_ms_p50: 12
kv_eviction_time_ms_p95: 150
kv_agebucket_0_1m: 400k
kv_agebucket_1m_10m: 300k
kv_agebucket_10m_1h: 80k
kv_agebucket_1h_plus: 12k
pagechain_avg_len: 3.1
pagechain_max_len: 87
```

kevin: interesting that agebucket 1h_plus is non-trivial. For a streaming chat session, we expect high short-lived entries. Could be a leak where some prefixes never expire because of tool loop references. Did you reproduce with prefix caching disabled?

maria (eng-runtime): repro steps I used:
1) start runtime with `--kv-ttl-seconds=3600 --prefix-cache=true --batcher=dynamic`
2) run agent harness: 100 concurrent sessions, each does repeated tool calls every 30s with ~1k tokens incremental context
3) let it run 16h, capture metrics every 5m

I did a short run with `--prefix-cache=false`, growth rate dropped to ~20MB/hr but did not fully stop. So prefix cache amplifies it but not sole cause.

olga: good hint. Could be combination: batcher dynamic holds onto KV refs longer (to preserve token locality), and kernel selection path for certain model/padding avoids copying leading to stale KV pointers in pools. Any allocator-specific diagnostics? tcmalloc vs jemalloc?

maria (eng-runtime): runtime built with jemalloc 5.3.0. I ran `jeprof` snapshot: dominant retained objects are small arenas of ~64B and some 512B blocks labelled "kv_slot_meta". Heaptrack shows many allocations associated with `kv_get_ref()` during tool calls.

kevin: hypothesis: when a batch contains a long context session, we hold onto its KV slices across microbatches. If batching heuristics prefer grouping similar seq-lengths, that could cause hot sessions to be kept alive and their pagechains pinned. Two asks: (1) try `--batcher=stateless` or set `max_batch_linger_ms=0` and re-run; (2) instrument KV to emit live-pointer-count per session id at 1m granularity.

maria (eng-runtime): tried `--batcher=stateless`, `max_batch_linger_ms=0` on a 4h run: growth dropped to ~10MB/hr. That strongly implicates batching heuristics. But there's still residual growth even with stateless, so there's at least one more leak path.

olga: can you get a heap profile when growth is still rising and when it plateaus? compare alloc stacks. Also check for ephemeral std::shared_ptr cycles in tool-loop glue code. We had a similar bug where callback closures held a SessionRef.

maria (eng-runtime): good call. Found a tiny vector of callbacks in ToolRunner that stores a lambda capturing `session->kv_view` for retries. Those closures are created per-tool-call but I thought we cleaned them up. The vector isn't cleared on success path for retries=0 (oops). Patch incoming.

kevin: nice catch. That'll explain part of the prefix-cache amplification: closures keep refs, preventing eviction. But what about pagechain_max_len 87? indicates fragmentation of pages, possibly partial page pin due to long-lived slices.

maria (eng-runtime): I force-ran a manual compaction (kv->compact_pages()) every 1hr in a test and that reduced pagechain_max_len to ~10 and growth stabilized. That's a mitigation but not a long-term fix.

olga: two-pronged fix plan: (A) patch ToolRunner to clear callback vector on success and ensure move semantics (PR in review), (B) add a background compaction pass that is leak-aware and runs when long-context sessions are detected (heuristic: if agebucket_1h_plus > threshold). Also add telemetry to expose live-ref counts per session in the console.

ci-bot: Build 2026.03.17.001 triggered by maria's PR. Tests: unit-kv, stress-longcontext. Status: queued.

kevin: let's also add a debug flag to make KV evict aggressively for sessions labeled `test-repro` so we can validate post-PR. maria, can you run that after CI?

maria (eng-runtime): will run CI, then reproduce with `--kv-eviction-aggressiveness=high --kv-evict-tag=test-repro`. Plan to collect a 24h run and upload pmap + jemalloc snapshots.

olga: follow-up: also consider that some kernel selection paths avoid copying KV to device memory for small models (zero-copy). That reduces latency but can keep host-side pointers alive longer. Add a trace when `kernel_choice==zero_copy` and correlate with pinned slot counts.

maria (eng-runtime): added kernel trace hook to the repro harness. Early numbers: sessions that hit zero_copy path have 2x pinned_slots on average. Will include that in write-up.

kevin: excellent. Once CI passes, let's schedule a 30m sync to decide whether compaction should be auto-enabled or opt-in. Thanks for the thorough triage, @olga for the callback theory. :clap:

maria (eng-runtime): PRs: toolrunner-callback-clear (in review), kv-compaction-heuristic (draft). I'll post links after CI. Closing thread for now, will reopen if further spikes after deploying the fix to staging.
